items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: I can remember one night Albert Ammons, the (inaudible) Boogie-woogie pianist (inaudible) came in. Barney was standing at the door, and Albert spoke to him. Barney didn't answer him, and he came back to the dressing room crying (inaudible). And we gave him hell.

ctx.x: Downtown, we had the boogie-woogie pianists Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons and Joe Turner and a comedian, various ones, and then we went uptown we had Mildred Bailey, Savo --
